name: Lumineers / no-prep veneers

lead: No-prep veneers are ultra-thin porcelain shells intended to need little or no filing of the natural tooth. Lumineers is a well-known brand name. They change colour and shape and are used for discolouration, shape and enamel defects, with the result visible as soon as they are placed.

A thin porcelain layer is bonded to etched enamel, which is why less tooth reduction may be needed. Dental sources describe conventional porcelain veneers as typically lasting 10 to 30 years, and proponents of the minimal-grinding approach emphasise preserving enamel. A general encyclopedia article describes non-prep veneers this way but flags the claim as needing a better source.

paras: People book a cosmetic dentist, who takes impressions, has the shells made in a lab and bonds them over the front teeth, usually across a couple of visits. They are often chosen for a whole-smile makeover and sometimes combined with whitening beforehand to set the target shade.

Veneers in general can chip, crack, leak or discolour, and can cause sensitivity and decay. One study cited in an encyclopedia article reported half of veneers unsatisfactory after 10 years. Preparation by an inexperienced dentist can remove a significant share of tooth surface.

angle.text: Users consider Lumineers and other no-prep veneers, ultra-thin porcelain shells needing little or no tooth reduction, to change tooth colour and shape. The change is visible as soon as they are bonded on, for a whiter, more uniform smile. The no-prep claim is flagged in general references as needing a better source.

lead: No-prep veneers are ultra-thin porcelain veneers placed with little or no reduction of natural tooth structure, and Lumineers is the commercial brand most associated with the category. People use them to change the colour, shape, length or spacing of visible front teeth, for a brighter and more even smile, while keeping more of their own enamel than conventional veneers require.[1][2][3]

The manufacturer describes its porcelain veneers as about as thin as a contact lens, says placement typically involves no shots or aggressive drilling, and states that they can be removed by a licensed dentist to reveal the original teeth. It says they are made in Lompoc, California, and have been sold under the Lumineers brand since 2004.[2] Wikipedia describes ultra-thin veneers needing little or no reduction but flags that claim as needing a better source.[1]

Dental sources describe conventional porcelain veneers as typically lasting 10 to 30 years, with preparation that, if done by an inexperienced dentist, can remove a significant share of tooth surface.[1] Cosmetic dentistry sources note that removed enamel cannot be replaced.[3]
infobox: Thin porcelain veneer, minimal or no tooth reduction
About as thin as a contact lens; made in Lompoc, California[2]

paras: Veneers are thin layers placed over the tooth surface, mainly for appearance, and are indicated for discolouration, malformation, enamel defects, fluorosis, fractures, wear and shape changes.[1] Porcelain veneers are made indirectly in a laboratory, while composite can be built up directly in the mouth.[1] Laminate veneers cover only the front surface, while veneer crowns cover all visible and biting surfaces.[1]

Cosmetic dentistry sources describe conventional veneers as thin custom porcelain shells that close gaps, reshape teeth or change colour and that usually require some tooth reduction, with dentists often making a wax or temporary mock-up first so the patient can preview the result.[3] No-prep designs aim to skip or minimise that reduction step.

Veneers were created in 1928 by California dentist Charles Pincus for a film shoot, to temporarily change actors' teeth, and he made acrylic versions in 1937. Etching of enamel was introduced by Michael Buonocore in 1959, and in 1982 Simonsen and Calamia showed porcelain could be etched with hydrofluoric acid to enable durable bonding.[1] Multiple upper-tooth veneers are used for 'Hollywood' smile makeovers.[1]

Wikipedia reports composite veneers lasting about four years and modern veneers typically 10 to 30 years, with one cited study finding about half displaced, needing re-treatment or unsatisfactory after 10 years; it also notes that the survival-rate citation is weak.[1] US costs were about $1,000 to $3,000 per tooth as of 2011.[1]

Contraindications listed for veneers include poor oral hygiene, uncontrolled gum disease, high cavity rate, grinding, absent enamel, unrealistic expectations and large existing restorations.[1] Sensitivity and decay can occur even when the procedure is done properly.[1] Critics warn against using veneers for 'instant orthodontics' on healthy teeth.[1]

The American Dental Association does not recognise cosmetic dentistry as a formal specialty, so any dentist can use the title 'cosmetic dentist'; Wikipedia cites debate about whether general dentists should take on complex smile makeovers.[3] Lumineers must be placed by a licensed dentist.[2]
No studies found that evaluate no-prep veneers or the Lumineers brand specifically.
